    #  in creation order
    hiding: list[tuple[float, bool]] = dataclasses.field(default_factory=list)

    def hidden(self, layer: int) -> bool:
        """Check whether a tile layer is drawn while hiding.

        Tiles draw after instances of their depth, so what counts is the
        last marker drawn before them: the shallowest one at or deeper than
        the layer, the latest created among equally deep ones.
        """
        before = [
            (depth, idx, start)
            for idx, (depth, start) in enumerate(self.hiding)
            if depth >= layer
        ]
        if not before:
            return False
        return min(before, key=lambda m: (m[0], -m[1]))[2]


def is_tile_layer_file(file: Path) -> bool:
    """Check whether a room file is a tile layer (named by its depth)."""
    return file.suffix == '.txt' and file.stem.removeprefix('-').isdigit()

# see ex1.3 - Clusters
assets: list[Asset] = ...

root = cfg.project.root
objects = {
    asset.name: asset
    for asset in assets
    if isinstance(asset, my_asset.Object)
}
metas = {
    name: obj.get_object_metadata(root) for name, obj in objects.items()
}

def descends(name: str, ancestors: frozenset[str]) -> bool:
    seen: set[str] = set()
    while name and name not in seen:
        if name in ancestors:
            return True
        seen.add(name)
        meta = metas.get(name)
        name = meta.parent if meta else ''
    return False

layer_call = re.compile(
    r'\btile_layer_(?:hide|show|shift|delete|delete_at|depth)\s*\(\s*'
    r'(-?\d+)\s*[,)]'
)

def literal_depths(file: Path) -> set[int]:
    if not file.exists():
        return set()
    text = file.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
    return {int(m.group(1)) for m in layer_call.finditer(text)}

object_depths = {
    name: literal_depths(obj.get_object_gml_file(root))
    for name, obj in objects.items()
}
depth_field = re.compile(
    r'^\s*depth\s*=\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)', re.MULTILINE
)

protection: dict[str, TileProtection] = {}
for room in assets:
    if not isinstance(room, my_asset.Room):
        continue
    folder = room.get_room_folder(root)
    prot = TileProtection()
    prot.tile_layers |= literal_depths(room.get_room_gml_file(root))
    instances = folder / 'instances.txt'
    lines = (
        instances.read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines()
        if instances.exists()
        else []
    )
    for line in lines:
        if not line:
            continue
        fields = line.split(',')
        obj = fields[0]
        if obj == AUTO_LAYER_OBJECT:
            prot.auto_layer_ids.append(fields[3])
        prot.tile_layers |= object_depths.get(obj, set())
        finder = descends(obj, TILE_FINDERS)
        layer_user = descends(obj, TILE_LAYER_USERS)
        hiding = obj in {LAYER_HIDE_START, LAYER_HIDE_END}
        if not (finder or layer_user or hiding or obj == MODEL_OBJECT):
            continue
        # depth from creation code, or the object's
        depth = float(metas[obj].depth) if obj in metas else 0.0
        code = folder / f'{fields[3]}.gml'
        if code.exists():
            found = depth_field.findall(
                code.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
            )
            if found:
                depth = float(found[-1])
        layer = int(depth)
        if hiding:
            prot.hiding.append((depth, obj == LAYER_HIDE_START))
        elif finder:
            prot.points.setdefault(layer, []).append((
                float(fields[1]),
                float(fields[2]),
            ))
        elif layer_user:
            prot.fixed_layers.add(layer)
        else:
            prot.tile_layers.add(layer)
    protection[room.name] = prot

log.info(
    'Protected: %d layers fixed, %d kept as tiles, %d tile positions',
    sum(len(p.fixed_layers) for p in protection.values()),
    sum(len(p.tile_layers) for p in protection.values()),
    sum(len(v) for p in protection.values() for v in p.points.values()),
)

items.title: Example 4.6 - Juicer: texture atlas
items.text:
Pack tiles into texture atlases, and bake them into models.

Fewer textures and draw calls per room, by rewriting room tile layers:

  1. Only backgrounds referenced from nothing but room tile layers qualify: room tiles point to a region of a background, so they can point to a region of an atlas page instead. Others stay as they are.
  2. Tiles of those get their transparent edges cropped (fully transparent ones are dropped). Large ones are split into cells: empty cells are dropped, single color ones are drawn with a white patch, stretched and tinted, and the rest merge back into as few rectangles as possible. Tiles stay where they were drawn, also when scaled or mirrored; tiles whose parts would land between pixels stay whole.
  3. Regions lying within others, or overlapping them closely enough, are stored once, and so are regions with identical pixels.
  4. Regions are packed onto pages of the cluster of their background (so pages load and unload with their stage), with a border repeating their edges, and tiles are pointed to the pages.
  5. Tiles of each layer are baked into models (shap_Model), one per texture where order allows. Tiles overlapping ones that have to stay tiles stay tiles too, so drawing order doesn't change.

Rooms with AUTO_LAYER_OBJECT get its models made here, in place of the object, which reads the room source at runtime (and only works in debug). Layers hidden by LAYER_HIDE_START/LAYER_HIDE_END are removed.

Protected tiles (see main_ex_tile_protection) are only pointed to pages, never changed otherwise. With crop_found_tiles, tiles found by position get their transparent edges cropped too, as long as they still cover that position. Original backgrounds stay in the project (so asset ids don't change), but aren't loaded anymore.

import concurrent.futures
import dataclasses
import hashlib
import itertools as it
import json
import logging
import re

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from rich import console as r_console

from clunkster import asset as my_asset
from clunkster import atlas as my_atlas
from clunkster import tiles as my_tiles
from clunkster.asset import Asset
from clunkster.parse import png as my_parse_png

# see ex0.1 - Setup: Config
class Config: ...

# see ex0.2 - Setup: Output
CONSOLE: r_console.Console = ...
log: logging.Logger = ...
def setup_output(): ...
def step(): ...
def progress(): ...
def render_table(): ...

# see ex1.3 - Clusters
def asset_cluster_raw(): ...
def asset_cluster(): ...

# see ex2.1 - Reference scanning
class Dependency: ...

# see ex4.5 - Juicer: protected tiles
class AtlasEntry: ...
class AtlasPage: ...
class ModelPlan: ...
class RoomPlan: ...
class Atlas: ...
class TileProtection: ...

# see ex1.3 - Clusters
assets: list[Asset] = ...

# see ex2.1 - Reference scanning
dependencies: list[Dependency] = ...

# see ex4.5 - Juicer: protected tiles
protection: dict[str, TileProtection] = ...

root = cfg.project.root
backgrounds = {
    asset.name: asset
    for asset in assets
    if isinstance(asset, my_asset.Background)
}
rooms = [asset for asset in assets if isinstance(asset, my_asset.Room)]

# backgrounds referenced from anything but room tiles stay as they are
excluded: set[str] = set()
for dep in dependencies:
    target = dep.target_asset
    if isinstance(target, my_asset.Background) and not (
        isinstance(dep.source_asset, my_asset.Room)
        and is_tile_layer_file(dep.location.file)
    ):
        excluded.add(target.name)

pixels: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

def image(name: str) -> np.ndarray:
    if name not in pixels:
        file = backgrounds[name].get_background_image(root)
        with Image.open(file) as img:
            pixels[name] = np.asarray(img.convert('RGBA'))
    return pixels[name]

# read layers
layers: dict[str, dict[int, list[my_tiles.Tile]]] = {}
for room in progress(rooms, 'Reading tiles'):
    layers[room.name] = {
        depth: my_tiles.parse_layer(
            room.get_room_layer_file(root, depth).read_text(
                encoding='utf-8'
            )
        )
        for depth in room.get_room_layers(root)
    }

# pick backgrounds: tiles must stay within them
candidates: set[str] = set()
used: dict[str, list[my_atlas.Rect]] = {}
for room_layers in layers.values():
    for tiles in room_layers.values():
        for tile in tiles:
            used.setdefault(tile.bg, []).append(tile.region())
for name, rects in used.items():
    bg = backgrounds.get(name)
    if bg is None or name in excluded:
        continue
    if not bg.get_background_image(root).exists():
        continue
    height, width = image(name).shape[:2]
    if all(
        left >= 0
        and top >= 0
        and 0 < w <= ATLAS_PAGE_SIZE - 2 * ATLAS_BORDER
        and 0 < h <= ATLAS_PAGE_SIZE - 2 * ATLAS_BORDER
        and left + w <= width
        and top + h <= height
        for left, top, w, h in rects
    ):
        candidates.add(name)
    else:
        log.warning('Not atlasing %s: tiles reach outside of it', name)

# region -> parts
part_cache: dict[tuple[str, my_atlas.Rect], list[AtlasPart]] = {}

def crop(
    pix: np.ndarray, x: int, y: int, w: int, h: int
) -> AtlasPart | None:
    alpha = pix[y : y + h, x : x + w, 3]
    cols = np.flatnonzero(alpha.any(axis=0))
    rows = np.flatnonzero(alpha.any(axis=1))
    if not cols.size:
        return None
    return (
        x + int(cols[0]),
        y + int(rows[0]),
        int(cols[-1] - cols[0]) + 1,
        int(rows[-1] - rows[0]) + 1,
        None,
    )

def crop_tile(tile: my_tiles.Tile) -> my_tiles.Tile | None:
    """Crop a tile's transparent edges, ``None`` if it's all transparent.

    Crop offsets are snapped outwards so that the tile stays on whole
    pixels when scaled (e.g. multiples of 5 for scale 0.8).
    """
    left, top, width, height = tile.region()
    part = crop(
        image(tile.bg)[top : top + height, left : left + width],
        0,
        0,
        width,
        height,
    )
    if part is None:
        return None
    dx, dy, w, h, _ = part
    snapped_dx = _snap_offset(dx, tile.xscale)
    snapped_dy = _snap_offset(dy, tile.yscale)
    return tile.sub(
        snapped_dx, snapped_dy, w + dx - snapped_dx, h + dy - snapped_dy
    )

def crop_found(
    room_name: str,
    depth: int,
    tile: my_tiles.Tile,
    found_at: list[tuple[float, float]],
) -> my_tiles.Tile:
    """Crop a tile found by position, if it still covers the position."""
    cropped = crop_tile(tile)
    if cropped is not None and all(it.starmap(cropped.contains, found_at)):
        return cropped
    log.warning(
        '%s, depth %d: kept tile %s whole, its SmartTile at %s is on %s',
        room_name,
        depth,
        tile.format(),
        ' '.join(f'{x:g},{y:g}' for x, y in found_at),
        'a fully transparent tile'
        if cropped is None
        else 'transparent pixels at its edge',
    )
    return tile

def parts(name: str, rect: my_atlas.Rect) -> list[AtlasPart]:
    key = (name, rect)
    if key in part_cache:
        return part_cache[key]
    left, top, width, height = rect
    pix = image(name)[top : top + height, left : left + width]
    whole = crop(pix, 0, 0, width, height)
    result: list[AtlasPart] = [] if whole is None else [whole]
    if whole is not None and min(whole[2], whole[3]) >= SPLIT_MIN_SIZE:
        cells: dict[tuple[int, int], int | None] = {}
        for cy in range(0, height, SPLIT_CELL):
            for cx in range(0, width, SPLIT_CELL):
                cell = pix[cy : cy + SPLIT_CELL, cx : cx + SPLIT_CELL]
                if not cell[..., 3].any():
                    continue
                first = cell[0, 0]
                if (cell == first).all():
                    r, g, b, a = (int(c) for c in first)
                    cells[cx // SPLIT_CELL, cy // SPLIT_CELL] = (
                        a << 24 | b << 16 | g << 8 | r
                    )
                else:
                    cells[cx // SPLIT_CELL, cy // SPLIT_CELL] = None
        split: list[AtlasPart] = []
        for cx, cy, cw, ch, color in my_atlas.grid_rects(cells):
            x, y = cx * SPLIT_CELL, cy * SPLIT_CELL
            w = min(cw * SPLIT_CELL, width - x)
            h = min(ch * SPLIT_CELL, height - y)
            if color is not None:
                split.append((x, y, w, h, color))
                continue
            part = crop(pix, x, y, w, h)
            if part is not None:
                split.append(part)
        kept = sum(p[2] * p[3] for p in split if p[4] is None)
        if kept <= (1 - SPLIT_MIN_GAIN) * whole[2] * whole[3]:
            result = split
    part_cache[key] = result
    return result

def on_pixels(tile: my_tiles.Tile, dx: int, dy: int) -> bool:
    return (dx * tile.xscale).is_integer() and (
        dy * tile.yscale
    ).is_integer()

# 1-2: crop and split, tiles keep the background they came from
new_layers: dict[str, dict[int, list[tuple[my_tiles.Tile, str]]]] = {}
protected: dict[str, dict[int, set[int]]] = {}
solid_clusters: set[str] = set()
for room_name, room_layers in layers.items():
    prot = protection.get(room_name, TileProtection())
    for depth, tiles in room_layers.items():
        if prot.hidden(depth) and not (
            prot.auto_layer_ids and depth > AUTO_LAYER_MIN_DEPTH
        ):
            # never shows, gets removed
            new_layers.setdefault(room_name, {})[depth] = []
            protected.setdefault(room_name, {})[depth] = set()
            continue
        points = prot.points.get(depth, [])
        keep: set[int] = set()
        out: list[tuple[my_tiles.Tile, str]] = []
        for tile in tiles:
            found_at = [pt for pt in points if tile.contains(*pt)]
            fixed = depth in prot.fixed_layers or bool(found_at)
            if (
                found_at
                and depth not in prot.fixed_layers
                and cfg.juicer.crop_found_tiles
                and tile.bg in candidates
            ):
                tile = crop_found(room_name, depth, tile, found_at)
            tile_parts = (
                None
                if fixed or tile.bg not in candidates
                else parts(tile.bg, tile.region())
            )
            if tile_parts is None:
                if fixed:
                    keep.add(len(out))
                out.append((tile, tile.bg))
                continue
            if not all(
                _on_pixel(p[0] * tile.xscale)
                and _on_pixel(p[1] * tile.yscale)
                for p in tile_parts
            ):
                # parts would land between pixels, crop it whole instead
                #  (snapping parts could make them overlap)
                cropped = crop_tile(tile)
                if cropped is not None:
                    out.append((cropped, tile.bg))
                continue
            for x, y, w, h, color in tile_parts:
                piece = tile.sub(x, y, w, h)
                if color is not None:
                    # white patch, stretched and tinted
                    piece = dataclasses.replace(
                        piece,
                        bg=ATLAS_WHITE,
                        left=0,
                        top=0,
                        width=ATLAS_WHITE_SIZE,
                        height=ATLAS_WHITE_SIZE,
                        xscale=w * tile.xscale / ATLAS_WHITE_SIZE,
                        yscale=h * tile.yscale / ATLAS_WHITE_SIZE,
                        color=tint(tile.color, color),
                    )
                    solid_clusters.add(
                        asset_cluster(cfg, backgrounds[tile.bg])
                    )
                out.append((piece, tile.bg))
        new_layers.setdefault(room_name, {})[depth] = out
        protected.setdefault(room_name, {})[depth] = keep

# 3: regions to store, per background; regions within or close to
#  others are stored as part of them, identical ones once
regions: dict[str, set[my_atlas.Rect]] = {}
for room_layers in new_layers.values():
    for tiles_from in room_layers.values():
        for tile, _ in tiles_from:
            if tile.bg in candidates:
                regions.setdefault(tile.bg, set()).add(tile.region())
# (background, region) -> its container, and where that's stored (the
#  container itself, or one with identical pixels in the same cluster)
stored_as: dict[
    tuple[str, my_atlas.Rect],
    tuple[my_atlas.Rect, tuple[str, my_atlas.Rect]],
] = {}
by_pixels: dict[tuple[str, bytes], tuple[str, my_atlas.Rect]] = {}
for name in sorted(regions):
    cluster = asset_cluster(cfg, backgrounds[name])
    merged = my_atlas.merge_regions(regions[name], ATLAS_MAX_MERGE_WASTE)
    for rect, container in sorted(merged.items()):
        left, top, w, h = container
        digest = hashlib.md5(
            image(name)[top : top + h, left : left + w].tobytes()
            + f'{w}x{h}'.encode()
        ).digest()
        stored_as[name, rect] = (
            container,
            by_pixels.setdefault((cluster, digest), (name, container)),
        )

# 4: pack per cluster, pages get a white patch if needed
by_cluster: dict[str, set[tuple[str, my_atlas.Rect]]] = {}
for _, (name, rect) in stored_as.values():
    cluster = asset_cluster(cfg, backgrounds[name])
    by_cluster.setdefault(cluster, set()).add((name, rect))
for cluster in solid_clusters:
    by_cluster.setdefault(cluster, set())
border = ATLAS_BORDER
white_size = ATLAS_WHITE_SIZE + 2 * border
pages: list[AtlasPage] = []
placed: dict[tuple[str, my_atlas.Rect], tuple[str, int, int]] = {}
white: dict[str, tuple[str, int, int]] = {}
# packing is slow: results are cached by input in the build folder, and
#  packed in parallel otherwise
jobs: dict[
    str, tuple[list[tuple[str, my_atlas.Rect]], str, AtlasPackJob]
] = {}
for cluster, stored in sorted(by_cluster.items()):
    keys = sorted(stored, key=lambda k: (-k[1][2] * k[1][3], k))
    job = (
        [(r[2] + 2 * border, r[3] + 2 * border) for _, r in keys],
        (white_size, white_size) if cluster in solid_clusters else None,
    )
    jobs[cluster] = (
        keys,
        hashlib.md5(repr(job).encode()).hexdigest(),
        job,
    )
file_pack_cache = cfg.juicer.dir_out / 'clunkster_atlas_pack.json'
pack_cache: dict[str, AtlasPackedPages] = {}
if file_pack_cache.exists():
    pack_cache.update(
        json.loads(file_pack_cache.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    )
missing = [c for c, (_, key, _) in jobs.items() if key not in pack_cache]
if missing:
    log.info('Packing %d cluster(s)', len(missing))
    with concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor() as pool:
        for cluster, packed_pages in zip(
            missing,
            pool.map(_atlas_pack_job, [jobs[c][2] for c in missing]),
            strict=True,
        ):
            pack_cache[jobs[cluster][1]] = packed_pages
file_pack_cache.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
write_if_changed(
    file_pack_cache,
    json.dumps({key: pack_cache[key] for _, key, _ in jobs.values()}),
)

for cluster, (keys, key, _) in jobs.items():
    packed = pack_cache[key]
    prefix = re.sub(r'\W', '_', cluster)
    for idx, (page_width, page_height, members) in enumerate(packed):
        page_name = f'__atlas_{prefix}_{idx}'
        if page_name in backgrounds:
            raise ValueError(f'Atlas page name {page_name} is taken')
        entries: list[AtlasEntry] = []
        for item, x, y in members:
            if item is None:
                entry = AtlasEntry(
                    ATLAS_WHITE,
                    0,
                    0,
                    ATLAS_WHITE_SIZE,
                    ATLAS_WHITE_SIZE,
                    x=x + border,
                    y=y + border,
                )
                white.setdefault(cluster, (page_name, entry.x, entry.y))
            else:
                name, rect = keys[item]
                entry = AtlasEntry(name, *rect, x=x + border, y=y + border)
                placed[keys[item]] = (page_name, entry.x, entry.y)
            entries.append(entry)
        asset = my_asset.Background(
            name=page_name,
            # root assets are Common
            tree_path=() if cluster == 'Common' else (cluster,),
        )
        pages.append(
            AtlasPage(asset, page_width, page_height, tuple(entries))
        )

def to_page(tile: my_tiles.Tile, source: str) -> my_tiles.Tile:
    if tile.bg == ATLAS_WHITE:
        page, x, y = white[asset_cluster(cfg, backgrounds[source])]
        return dataclasses.replace(tile, bg=page, left=x, top=y)
    if tile.bg not in candidates:
        return tile
    container, key = stored_as[tile.bg, tile.region()]
    page, x, y = placed[key]
    return dataclasses.replace(
        tile,
        bg=page,
        left=x + tile.left - container[0],
        top=y + tile.top - container[1],
    )

# 5: bake
page_sizes = {p.asset.name: (p.width, p.height) for p in pages}
texture_sizes: dict[str, tuple[int, int] | None] = {}

def texture_size(name: str) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    if name in page_sizes:
        return page_sizes[name]
    if name not in texture_sizes:
        bg = backgrounds.get(name)
        file = bg.get_background_image(root) if bg else None
        texture_sizes[name] = (
            my_parse_png.size(file) if file and file.exists() else None
        )
    return texture_sizes[name]

plans: dict[str, RoomPlan] = {}
tiles_before = tiles_after = models_after = 0
for room in rooms:
    prot = protection.get(room.name, TileProtection())
    changed: dict[int, tuple[my_tiles.Tile, ...]] = {}
    models: list[ModelPlan] = []
    auto_models: list[ModelPlan] = []
    for depth, tiles_from in new_layers.get(room.name, {}).items():
        original = layers[room.name][depth]
        mapped = list(it.starmap(to_page, tiles_from))
        if prot.auto_layer_ids and depth > AUTO_LAYER_MIN_DEPTH:
            # what AUTO_LAYER_OBJECT does at runtime: the whole layer
            #  as models at a shallower depth
            auto_models.extend(
                _bake_layer(
                    cfg,
                    room.name,
                    depth,
                    # all tiles, like the object
                    [t for t in mapped if texture_size(t.bg) is not None],
                    texture_size,
                    kind='auto',
                    model_depth=depth - AUTO_LAYER_OFFSET,
                )
            )
        if prot.hidden(depth):
            # never shows: removed (after auto layers took its tiles)
            tiles_before += len(original)
            changed[depth] = ()
            continue
        keep = set(protected[room.name][depth])
        if depth not in prot.tile_layers | prot.fixed_layers:
            # tiles reaching outside of their texture stay tiles, models
            #  would wrap around instead
            keep |= {
                i
                for i, tile in enumerate(mapped)
                if not _within_texture(tile, texture_size(tile.bg))
            }
            keep = _overlap_closure(mapped, keep)
            layer_models = _bake_layer(
                cfg,
                room.name,
                depth,
                [t for i, t in enumerate(mapped) if i not in keep],
                texture_size,
            )
            models.extend(layer_models)
            models_after += len(layer_models)
            mapped = [t for i, t in enumerate(mapped) if i in keep]
        tiles_before += len(original)
        tiles_after += len(mapped)
        if mapped != original:
            changed[depth] = tuple(mapped)
    if changed or models or prot.auto_layer_ids:
        plans[room.name] = RoomPlan(
            layers=changed,
            models=tuple(models),
            auto_layer_ids=tuple(prot.auto_layer_ids),
            auto_models=tuple(auto_models),
        )

# every tile of these points to pages now
atlased = frozenset(candidates)
log.info(
    'Packed regions of %d background(s) into %d page(s): %s',
    len(atlased),
    len(pages),
    ', '.join(f'{p.asset.name} {p.width}x{p.height}' for p in pages),
)
log.info(
    'Tiles: %d -> %d tiles and %d models',
    tiles_before,
    tiles_after,
    models_after,
)

Packing, baking, page composition and room rewriting are done by these; pages and rooms are written by build tasks, so they're cached:

import collections.abc as col
import hashlib
import shutil
from pathlib import Path
from typing import override

import numpy as np
import rpack
from PIL import Image

from clunkster import model as my_model
from clunkster import tiles as my_tiles
from clunkster.pipeline import task as my_task

# see ex4.5 - Juicer: protected tiles
class AtlasEntry: ...
class AtlasPage: ...
class ModelPlan: ...
class RoomPlan: ...
class Atlas: ...
class TileProtection: ...

# see ex4.1 - Juicer: the juice
def juice_sprite(): ...
def juice_background(): ...
def juice_audio(): ...
def juice_obj_fix_mask(): ...

def tint(color: int, pixel: int) -> int:
    """Combine a tile color with a pixel color (both ARGB, BGR order).

    Channels multiply, like drawing the pixel with the tile color does.
    """
    channels = [
        round(((color >> shift) & 0xFF) * ((pixel >> shift) & 0xFF) / 255)
        for shift in (0, 8, 16, 24)
    ]
    return (
        channels[0] | channels[1] << 8 | channels[2] << 16 | channels[3] << 24
    )


# pages: width, height, rectangles (index or None for the extra one, x, y)
AtlasPackedPages = list[tuple[int, int, list[tuple[int | None, int, int]]]]
# sizes of rectangles, and the extra one
AtlasPackJob = tuple[list[tuple[int, int]], tuple[int, int] | None]


def atlas_pack_pages(
    sizes: col.Sequence[tuple[int, int]],
    extra: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
) -> AtlasPackedPages:
    """Pack rectangles onto as few pages as possible, with ``rpack``.

    Every page takes the longest run of the remaining rectangles (in the
    given order, largest first works best) that fits, so pages fill up.

    :param sizes: Rectangle sizes.
    :param extra: Rectangle added to every page, if any.
    :return: Pages: width, height and placed rectangles (index into
      ``sizes``, or ``None`` for the extra one, x, y).
    """

    def attempt(items: list[int]) -> list[tuple[int, int]] | None:
        rects = [sizes[i] for i in items]
        if extra is not None:
            rects.append(extra)
        try:
            return rpack.pack(
                rects, max_width=ATLAS_PAGE_SIZE, max_height=ATLAS_PAGE_SIZE
            )
        except rpack.PackingImpossibleError:
            return None

    extra_size = extra if extra is not None else (0, 0)
    pages: AtlasPackedPages = []
    remaining = list(range(len(sizes)))
    while remaining or (extra is not None and not pages):
        positions = attempt(remaining)
        count = len(remaining)
        if positions is None:
            # binary search the longest run that fits
            low, high = 1, len(remaining) - 1
            positions = attempt(remaining[:1])
            if positions is None:
                raise ValueError(f'{sizes[remaining[0]]} exceeds page size')
            count = 1
            while low <= high:
                middle = (low + high) // 2
                found = attempt(remaining[:middle])
                if found is None:
                    high = middle - 1
                else:
                    positions, count, low = found, middle, middle + 1
        items: list[int | None] = list(remaining[:count])
        if extra is not None:
            items.append(None)
        rects = [sizes[i] if i is not None else extra_size for i in items]
        width = max(
            x + r[0] for (x, _), r in zip(positions, rects, strict=True)
        )
        height = max(
            y + r[1] for (_, y), r in zip(positions, rects, strict=True)
        )
        pages.append((
            width,
            height,
            [
                (item, x, y)
                for item, (x, y) in zip(items, positions, strict=True)
            ],
        ))
        remaining = remaining[count:]
    return pages


def _within_texture(tile: my_tiles.Tile, size: tuple[int, int] | None) -> bool:
    """Check whether a tile's region lies within its texture."""
    return size is not None and (
        tile.left >= 0
        and tile.top >= 0
        and tile.left + tile.width <= size[0]
        and tile.top + tile.height <= size[1]
    )


def _atlas_pack_job(job: AtlasPackJob) -> AtlasPackedPages:
    """Run ``atlas_pack_pages`` (for process pools)."""
    return atlas_pack_pages(job[0], extra=job[1])


def _on_pixel(value: float) -> bool:
    """Check whether a position is a whole pixel (allowing float error)."""
    return abs(value - round(value)) < 1e-6


def _snap_offset(offset: int, scale: float) -> int:
    """Get the largest offset up to ``offset`` that's a whole pixel scaled."""
    while offset > 0 and not _on_pixel(offset * scale):
        offset -= 1
    return offset


def _overlaps(a: tuple[float, ...], b: tuple[float, ...]) -> bool:
    return a[0] < b[2] and b[0] < a[2] and a[1] < b[3] and b[1] < a[3]


def _overlap_closure(tiles: list[my_tiles.Tile], keep: set[int]) -> set[int]:
    """Extend kept tiles with tiles overlapping them, transitively.

    Kept tiles stay tiles while the rest becomes models drawn above them,
    so anything overlapping a kept tile has to stay a tile too.
    """
    keep = set(keep)
    bounds = [tile.bounds() for tile in tiles]
    new = list(keep)
    while new:
        added = [
            i
            for i in range(len(tiles))
            if i not in keep
            and any(_overlaps(bounds[i], bounds[k]) for k in new)
        ]
        keep.update(added)
        new = added
    return keep


def model_name(
    cfg: Config, room: str, depth: int, index: int, kind: str = ''
) -> str:
    """Name a baked model (file name in data/model).

    Scrambled by default, so the model folder doesn't show room names.
    """
    key = f'model/{room}/{depth}/{index}'
    if kind:
        key += f'/{kind}'
    if cfg.juicer.scramble_models or cfg.juicer.hash_names:
        digest = hashlib.blake2b(
            key.encode(), key=cfg.juicer.name_salt.encode(), digest_size=8
        ).hexdigest()
        return f'{digest.upper()}.g3z'
    suffix = f'__{kind}' if kind else ''
    return f'{room}__{depth}__{index}{suffix}.g3z'


def _bake_layer(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments]
    cfg: Config,
    room: str,
    depth: int,
    tiles: list[my_tiles.Tile],
    texture_size: col.Callable[[str], tuple[int, int] | None],
    *,
    kind: str = '',
    model_depth: float | None = None,
) -> list[ModelPlan]:
    """Bake tiles of a layer into models, one per texture where possible.

    Models go just above the layer (see ``MODEL_DEPTH_STEP``), or all at
    ``model_depth``, ordered by creation then.

    A tile joins the latest model of its texture, unless a later model (of
    another texture) overlaps it: then drawing order would change, so it
    starts a new model.
    """
    groups: list[tuple[str, list[my_tiles.Tile], list[float]]] = []
    for tile in tiles:
        bounds = tile.bounds()
        target = None
        for texture, members, group_bounds in reversed(groups):
            if texture == tile.bg:
                target = (members, group_bounds)
                break
            if _overlaps(bounds, tuple(group_bounds)):
                break
        if target is None:
            groups.append((tile.bg, [], [*bounds]))
            target = (groups[-1][1], groups[-1][2])
        members, group_bounds = target
        members.append(tile)
        group_bounds[:] = [
            min(group_bounds[0], bounds[0]),
            min(group_bounds[1], bounds[1]),
            max(group_bounds[2], bounds[2]),
            max(group_bounds[3], bounds[3]),
        ]

    models: list[ModelPlan] = []
    for idx, (texture, members, _) in enumerate(groups):
        size = texture_size(texture)
        assert size is not None
        width, height = size
        quads = tuple(
            my_model.Quad(
                x1=t.x,
                y1=t.y,
                x2=t.x + t.width * t.xscale,
                y2=t.y + t.height * t.yscale,
                u1=t.left / width,
                v1=t.top / height,
                u2=(t.left + t.width) / width,
                v2=(t.top + t.height) / height,
                color=t.blend,
                alpha=t.alpha,
            )
            for t in members
        )
        models.append(
            ModelPlan(
                name=model_name(cfg, room, depth, idx, kind),
                texture=texture,
                depth=depth - MODEL_DEPTH_STEP * (idx + 1)
                if model_depth is None
                else model_depth,
                quads=quads,
            )
        )
    return models


def write_if_changed(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
    """Write a text file, unless it already has this content.

    Keeps file stats, and therefore the build cache, intact.
    """
    if path.exists() and path.read_text(encoding='utf-8') == text:
        return
    path.write_text(text, encoding='utf-8', newline='\n')


def atlas_compose(page: AtlasPage, images: dict[str, Path]) -> Image.Image:
    """Compose page image from background regions.

    :param page: Page to compose.
    :param images: Image files of the backgrounds.
    """
    border = ATLAS_BORDER
    out = Image.new('RGBA', (page.width, page.height))
    sources: dict[str, Image.Image] = {}
    for e in page.entries:
        if e.bg == ATLAS_WHITE:
            region = Image.new(
                'RGBA', (e.width, e.height), (255, 255, 255, 255)
            )
        else:
            if e.bg not in sources:
                with Image.open(images[e.bg]) as img:
                    sources[e.bg] = img.convert('RGBA')
            region = sources[e.bg].crop((
                e.left,
                e.top,
                e.left + e.width,
                e.top + e.height,
            ))
        if border:
            # repeat edge pixels outwards
            arr = np.pad(
                np.asarray(region),
                ((border, border), (border, border), (0, 0)),
                mode='edge',
            )
            region = Image.fromarray(arr, 'RGBA')
        out.paste(region, (e.x - border, e.y - border))
    return out


def _digest(value: object) -> str:
    return hashlib.md5(repr(value).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]


class TaskAtlasPage(my_task.TaskGeneric):
    """Compose an atlas page."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        page: AtlasPage,
        images: dict[str, Path],
        file_png: Path | None,
        file_wet: Path | None,
        file_dump: Path | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the task.

        :param page: Page to compose.
        :param images: Image files of the backgrounds on the page.
        :param file_png: Page image to write, if any.
        :param file_wet: Wet page file to write, if any.
        :param file_dump: Page image to write for inspection, if any.
        """
        self.page = page
        self.images = {
            e.bg: images[e.bg] for e in page.entries if e.bg != ATLAS_WHITE
        }
        self.file_png = file_png
        self.file_wet = file_wet
        self.file_dump = file_dump
        super().__init__(
            # the layout is part of the id: changes to it rebuild the page
            task_id=f'atlas_page_{page.asset.name}_{_digest(page)}',
            inputs=tuple(sorted(set(self.images.values()))),
            outputs=tuple(
                f for f in (file_png, file_wet, file_dump) if f is not None
            ),
        )

    @override
    def execute(self) -> None:
        img = atlas_compose(self.page, self.images)
        if self.file_png is not None:
            img.save(self.file_png)
        if self.file_dump is not None:
            img.save(self.file_dump)
        if self.file_wet is not None:
            juice_background_image(
                meta=ATLAS_PAGE_META, img=img, out_file=self.file_wet
            )


def _instance_id(room: str, used: set[str], key: str) -> str:
    """Pick an instance id (8 hex digits) unique within the room."""
    salt = 0
    while True:
        instance_id = hashlib.md5(f'{room}|{key}|{salt}'.encode()).hexdigest()
        instance_id = instance_id[:8].upper()
        if instance_id not in used:
            used.add(instance_id)
            return instance_id
        salt += 1


class TaskAtlasRoom(my_task.TaskGeneric):
    """Copy a room, applying its atlas plan.

    Changed tile layers are rewritten, models written into the model
    folder, and ``shap_Model`` instances added to draw them.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        dir_room: Path,
        dir_out: Path,
        dir_models: Path,
        plan: RoomPlan | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the task.

        :param dir_room: Room folder.
        :param dir_out: Output room folder.
        :param dir_models: Folder to write models into.
        :param plan: Room's plan, ``None`` to copy as is.
        """
        self.files = tuple(
            sorted(file for file in dir_room.rglob('*') if file.is_file())
        )
        self.dir_room = dir_room
        self.dir_out = dir_out
        self.dir_models = dir_models
        self.plan = plan

        # layers left without tiles are removed, like the room editor does
        self.empty_layers = (
            {depth for depth, tiles in plan.layers.items() if not tiles}
            if plan is not None
            else set()
        )
        outputs = [
            dir_out / file.relative_to(dir_room)
            for file in self.files
            if self._layer_depth(file) not in self.empty_layers
        ]
        # instances of plan.models, then of plan.auto_models
        self.instance_ids: list[str] = []
        self.auto_instance_ids: list[str] = []
        if plan is not None and (plan.models or plan.auto_models):
            used = {
                line.split(',')[3]
                for line in (dir_room / 'instances.txt')
                .read_text(encoding='utf-8')
                .splitlines()
                if line
            }
            for models, ids in (
                (plan.models, self.instance_ids),
                (plan.auto_models, self.auto_instance_ids),
            ):
                for model in models:
                    instance_id = _instance_id(dir_room.name, used, model.name)
                    ids.append(instance_id)
                    outputs.extend((
                        dir_out / f'{instance_id}.gml',
                        dir_models / model.name,
                    ))
        super().__init__(
            # the plan is part of the id: changes to it rebuild the room
            task_id=f'atlas_room_{dir_room.name}_{_digest(plan)}',
            inputs=self.files,
            outputs=tuple(outputs),
        )

    def _instances(self, text: str) -> str:
        """Rewrite instances.txt with model instances.

        Models of auto layers replace the auto layer object (created at the
        same point, as it does at runtime), other models go last.
        """
        assert self.plan is not None
        auto = set(self.plan.auto_layer_ids)

        def line(instance_id: str) -> str:
            return f'{MODEL_OBJECT},0,0,{instance_id},0,1,1,4294967295,0,1'

        lines: list[str] = []
        for existing in text.splitlines():
            if not existing:
                continue
            if existing.split(',')[3] in auto:
                lines.extend(line(i) for i in self.auto_instance_ids)
                auto.clear()
                continue
            if existing.split(',')[0] == AUTO_LAYER_OBJECT:
                continue
            lines.append(existing)
        lines.extend(line(i) for i in self.instance_ids)
        return ''.join(f'{x}\n' for x in lines)

    def _layer_depth(self, file: Path) -> int | None:
        """Get depth of a tile layer file, ``None`` for other files."""
        if file.parent == self.dir_room and is_tile_layer_file(file):
            return int(file.stem)
        return None

    @override
    def execute(self) -> None:
        plan = self.plan
        layers = plan.layers if plan is not None else {}
        for depth in self.empty_layers:
            # left from an earlier build
            (self.dir_out / f'{depth}.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
        for file in self.files:
            out = self.dir_out / file.relative_to(self.dir_room)
            depth = self._layer_depth(file)
            if depth in self.empty_layers:
                continue
            if file.name == 'layers.txt' and self.empty_layers:
                kept = [
                    line
                    for line in file.read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines()
                    if line and int(line) not in self.empty_layers
                ]
                out.write_text(
                    ''.join(f'{line}\n' for line in kept),
                    encoding='utf-8',
                    newline='\n',
                )
            elif depth is not None and depth in layers:
                out.write_text(
                    my_tiles.format_layer(layers[depth]),
                    encoding='utf-8',
                    newline='\n',
                )
            elif file.name == 'instances.txt' and plan is not None:
                out.write_text(
                    self._instances(file.read_text(encoding='utf-8')),
                    encoding='utf-8',
                    newline='\n',
                )
            else:
                shutil.copy2(file, out)

        if plan is None:
            return
        for instance_id, model in zip(
            self.instance_ids + self.auto_instance_ids,
            plan.models + plan.auto_models,
            strict=True,
        ):
            (self.dir_out / f'{instance_id}.gml').write_text(
                '//gm82 fields begin\n'
                f'name="{model.name}"\n'
                f'tex_bg={model.texture}\n'
                f'depth={my_tiles.format_number(model.depth)}\n'
                '//gm82 fields end\n',
                encoding='utf-8',
                newline='\n',
            )
            (self.dir_models / model.name).write_bytes(
                my_model.model_g3z(model.quads)
            )

items.title: Example 4.7 - Juicer: lean builds
items.text:
Find exactly which assets lean rooms need.

Instead of whole clusters, rooms of lean clusters (or, in lean builds, every room) load what they actually reach (from the dependency graphs):

  • in lean builds, Common assets are loaded like any other; assets reached from global roots (EXTRA_ROOTS) in every room, unguarded, can't ever be unloaded: they stay in the executable, as do assets of persistent Common objects, which may follow the player anywhere
  • otherwise Common stays in the executable, as usual
  • assets of other persistent objects are needed in every room of their cluster, since they can outlive the room they were made in
  • with atlases, rooms need the pages their tiles were pointed to

:return: Config with resident set (lean builds), and needed assets per lean room.

import collections.abc as col
import dataclasses
import logging

import rustworkx as rx
from rich import console as r_console

from clunkster import asset as my_asset
from clunkster.asset import Asset

# see ex0.1 - Setup: Config
class Config: ...

# see ex0.2 - Setup: Output
CONSOLE: r_console.Console = ...
log: logging.Logger = ...
def setup_output(): ...
def step(): ...
def progress(): ...
def render_table(): ...

# see ex1.3 - Clusters
def asset_cluster_raw(): ...
def asset_cluster(): ...

# see ex4.1 - Juicer: the juice
def asset_resident(): ...

# see ex3.1 - Generate dependency graphs
class RoomGraph: ...

# see ex4.5 - Juicer: protected tiles
class AtlasEntry: ...
class AtlasPage: ...
class ModelPlan: ...
class RoomPlan: ...
class Atlas: ...
class TileProtection: ...

# see ex1.3 - Clusters
assets: list[Asset] = ...

# see ex3.1 - Generate dependency graphs
room_graph_data: dict[str, RoomGraph] = ...

root = cfg.project.root
lean_all = cfg.juicer.lean
by_name = {a.name: a for a in assets}
cluster_of = {a.name: asset_cluster(cfg, a) for a in assets}
loaded_types = (my_asset.Sprite, my_asset.Background, AssetExtAudio)
loadable = {a.name for a in assets if isinstance(a, loaded_types)}
persistent = [
    a.name
    for a in assets
    if isinstance(a, my_asset.Object)
    and a.get_object_metadata(root).persistent
    and a.name not in cfg.extra_roots
]
roots = set(cfg.extra_roots) | {
    name for name in persistent if cluster_of[name] == 'Common'
}

def reach(rg: RoomGraph, names: col.Iterable[str]) -> set[str]:
    found: set[str] = set()
    for name in names:
        if name in rg.name2index:
            idx = rg.name2index[name]
            found |= {rg.graph[i] for i in rx.descendants(rg.graph, idx)}
            found.add(name)
    return found & loadable

if lean_all:
    # resident: what roots reach in every room
    resident = set(loadable)
    for rg in room_data.values():
        resident &= reach(rg, roots)
    cfg = dataclasses.replace(cfg, resident=frozenset(resident))
lean_rooms = {
    name: rg
    for name, rg in room_data.items()
    if lean_all or cluster_of[name] in cfg.lean_clusters
}
lean_clusters = {cluster_of[name] for name in lean_rooms}

# persistent stage objects: whole cluster (reached as in their rooms)
by_cluster: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
for name in persistent:
    cluster = cluster_of[name]
    if name in roots or cluster not in lean_clusters:
        continue
    rg = next(
        (rg for n, rg in lean_rooms.items() if cluster_of[n] == cluster),
        None,
    )
    if rg is not None:
        by_cluster.setdefault(cluster, set()).update(reach(rg, [name]))
        if not lean_all:
            log.info('Persistent %s is loaded in all of %s', name, cluster)

atlased = atlas.atlased if atlas is not None else frozenset()
page_names = (
    {p.asset.name for p in atlas.pages} if atlas is not None else set()
)
needs: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
for room_name, rg in lean_rooms.items():
    need = rg.reachable_names & loadable
    need |= by_cluster.get(cluster_of[room_name], set())
    need = {
        n for n in need - atlased if not asset_resident(cfg, by_name[n])
    }
    plan = atlas.rooms.get(room_name) if atlas is not None else None
    if plan is not None:
        need |= {
            tile.bg
            for tiles in plan.layers.values()
            for tile in tiles
            if tile.bg in page_names
        }
        need |= {
            model.texture
            for model in plan.models + plan.auto_models
            if model.texture in page_names
        }
    needs[room_name] = need

def megabytes(names: col.Iterable[str]) -> float:
    return (
        sum(
            asset_ram_estimate(cfg, by_name[n])
            for n in names
            if n in by_name
        )
        / 2**20
    )

sizes = sorted(megabytes(need) for need in needs.values())
if cfg.resident is not None:
    log.info(
        'Resident: %d assets (~%.1f MB)',
        len(cfg.resident),
        megabytes(cfg.resident),
    )
log.info(
    'Lean rooms: %d; per room: median ~%.1f MB, max ~%.1f MB',
    len(needs),
    sizes[len(sizes) // 2] if sizes else 0,
    sizes[-1] if sizes else 0,
)

items.title: Example 4.8 - Juicer: package
items.text:
Pack the game into a zip.

The zip holds the compiled exe, named after the project, and the data folder (wet assets, stubs and whatever else the game loads from there).

import logging
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

from rich import console as r_console

# see ex0.1 - Setup: Config
class Config: ...

# see ex0.2 - Setup: Output
CONSOLE: r_console.Console = ...
log: logging.Logger = ...
def setup_output(): ...
def step(): ...
def progress(): ...
def render_table(): ...

# see ex4.1 - Juicer: the juice
class ConfJuicer: ...
JUICER: ConfJuicer = ...

dir_out = cfg.juicer.dir_out
name = Path(cfg.juicer.fname_gm82).stem
file_zip = dir_out / f'{name}.zip'
data_files = sorted(
    file for file in (dir_out / 'data').rglob('*') if file.is_file()
)
# already compressed formats aren't worth deflating
stored_suffixes = {'.ogg', '.mp3', '.png', '.jpg', '.zip'}

file_temp = file_zip.with_suffix('.tmp')
with zipfile.ZipFile(
    file_temp, 'w', compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
) as archive:
    archive.write(dir_out / 'game.exe', f'{name}.exe')
    for file in progress(data_files, 'Packaging'):
        archive.write(
            file,
            file.relative_to(dir_out).as_posix(),
            compress_type=zipfile.ZIP_STORED
            if file.suffix.lower() in stored_suffixes
            else zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED,
        )
file_temp.replace(file_zip)
log.info(
    'Packaged %s (%.1f MB)', file_zip, file_zip.stat().st_size / 2**20
)

items.title: Overview
items.text:
• clunkster - Separate Game Maker 8.2 projects into clusters.

    • clunkster.asset - Abstract asset type and builtin definitions.

    • clunkster.atlas - Texture atlas geometry.

    • clunkster.lint - Linter primitives: rules, violations and their reports.

      The library doesn't print or raise anything by itself; the pipeline ...

      collects violations, formats them with format_report and decides what to do with errors.

    • clunkster.model - GameMaker models (d3d_model_*).

    • clunkster.project - Source project.

    • clunkster.tiles - Room tile layers.

    • clunkster.analyze - Project analysis routines.

      Facilitates building dependency graph.

      • clunkster.analyze.scan_cache - Per-file cache of reference scan results.

      • clunkster.analyze.scan_dep - Routines for scanning text files for dependencies.

    • clunkster.parse - GameMaker8.2's text data parsing.

      • clunkster.parse.csv - Parse CSV-like metadata files into dataclasses.

      • clunkster.parse.gml - GML script static analysis.

        The purpose of the analysis is to find "guard scripts", like this: ... 

        if room_is_stageA() {
    ...
}
        anything inside this should be considered as only "referrable" if current room is a part of stageA cluster.

      • clunkster.parse.index - Parse index.yyd files.

      • clunkster.parse.kv - Parse GameMaker 8.2 key=value metadata files.

      • clunkster.parse.png - Read PNG metadata.

      • clunkster.parse.tree - Parse tree.yyd files.

    • clunkster.pipeline - Pipeline bones.

      Contains tasks, build cache and task execution.

      • clunkster.pipeline.cache - Build progress caching.

      • clunkster.pipeline.run - Task execution.

      • clunkster.pipeline.task - Pipeline task.

    • clunkster.text - Generic text tools.

      • clunkster.text.line - Source line map.

      • clunkster.text.location - Source navigation model.

items.title: DTC Asset
items.text:
Abstract asset.

Asset type must provide general asset type name, a way to check whether this specific asset type is used in the project, as well as a way to scan for all assets of this type in the given project.

View source 
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Asset(ABC):
    """Abstract asset.

    Asset type must provide general asset type name, a way to check
    whether this specific asset type is used in the project, as well as
    a way to scan for all assets of this type in the given project.
    """

    # name is the identifier by which the asset is referenced in GML code;
    #  it is also used as a primary key of the asset, so unique assets
    #  must have unique names
    name: str

    @classmethod
    @abstractmethod
    def type_name(cls) -> str:
        """Internal name of this asset type."""

    @classmethod
    @abstractmethod
    def type_is_used(cls, project_root: pl.Path) -> bool:
        """Check whether this asset type is used in the project or not."""

    @classmethod
    @abstractmethod
    def type_discover_all(cls, project_root: pl.Path) -> col.Iterator[Self]:
        """Iterate through assets of this type."""

    @classmethod
    def type_discover_names(cls, project_root: pl.Path) -> col.Iterator[str]:
        """Iterate through asset names of this type.

        Default implementation uses ``type_discover_all``, however,
        things like builtin assets should use ``index.yyd`` files.
        """
        return (asset.name for asset in cls.type_discover_all(project_root))

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AssetHasDir(Asset, ABC):
    """Asset mixin: type has a file directory in the project.

    Existence of this asset type in the project is determined by presence of
    its directory.

    @classmethod

        """Get directory of this asset type relative to project root."""

        """Get directory of this asset type.

        return project_root / cls.type_get_dir_rel()

    @classmethod
    def type_is_used(cls, project_root: pl.Path) -> bool:
        return cls.type_get_dir(project_root).exists()

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AssetSingleFile(AssetHasPath, AssetHasDir, ABC):
    """Abstract external asset, represented by a single file.

    Such files must be stored in dedicated folder, and assume structure in
    this folder would be used as tree paths.
    """

    file: pl.Path

    @classmethod
    @abstractmethod
    def type_globs(cls) -> col.Iterable[str]:
        """Get globs of the asset files.

        Used for asset discovery and is passed into ``rglob``.
        """
        return '*'

    @classmethod
    def type_file_to_asset_name(cls, file: pl.Path) -> str:
        """Convert file path to asset name.

        Assumes asset name to file's stem as a string. When overriding this
        method, make sure to also update ``name_clean`` property.
        """
        return f'"{file.stem}"'

    @property
    def name_clean(self) -> str:
        """Clean version of the asset name without quotes."""
        return self.name[1:-1]

    @classmethod
    def type_file_to_tree_path(
        cls, project_root: pl.Path, file: pl.Path
    ) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Convert file to tree path."""
        return file.relative_to(cls.type_get_dir(project_root)).parts[:-1]

    @override
    @classmethod
    def type_discover_all(cls, project_root: pl.Path) -> col.Iterator[Self]:
        """Discover assets of this asset type.

        Uses ``rglob`` with globs acquired from ``type_globs``.
        """
        asset_dir = cls.type_get_dir(project_root)

        file_iterator: col.Iterable[pl.Path] = it.chain.from_iterable(
            asset_dir.rglob(rglob) for rglob in cls.type_globs()
        )
        return (
            cls(
                name=cls.type_file_to_asset_name(file),
                tree_path=cls.type_file_to_tree_path(project_root, file),
                file=file,
            )
            for file in file_iterator
            if file.is_file()
        )

def rect_contains(outer: Rect, inner: Rect) -> bool:
    """Check whether ``inner`` lies fully within ``outer``."""
    return (
        outer[0] <= inner[0]
        and outer[1] <= inner[1]
        and inner[0] + inner[2] <= outer[0] + outer[2]
        and inner[1] + inner[3] <= outer[1] + outer[3]
    )

def rect_overlaps(a: Rect, b: Rect) -> bool:

def rect_bounds(rects: col.Iterable[Rect]) -> Rect:
    """Get the bounding rectangle."""
    rects = list(rects)
    left = min(r[0] for r in rects)
    top = min(r[1] for r in rects)
    right = max(r[0] + r[2] for r in rects)
    bottom = max(r[1] + r[3] for r in rects)
    return left, top, right - left, bottom - top

def union_area(
    rects: col.Sequence[Rect],
) -> int:

Get the area covered by rectangles (overlaps counted once).

View source 
def union_area(rects: col.Sequence[Rect]) -> int:
    """Get the area covered by rectangles (overlaps counted once)."""
    xs = sorted({x for r in rects for x in (r[0], r[0] + r[2])})
    area = 0
    for x1, x2 in it.pairwise(xs):
        spans = sorted(
            (r[1], r[1] + r[3])
            for r in rects
            if r[0] <= x1 and x2 <= r[0] + r[2]
        )
        covered = 0
        end = None
        for top, bottom in spans:
            if end is None or top > end:
                covered += bottom - top
                end = bottom
            elif bottom > end:
                covered += bottom - end
                end = bottom
        area += covered * (x2 - x1)
    return area

def merge_regions(
    rects: col.Iterable[Rect],
    max_waste: float,
) -> dict[Rect, Rect]:

Decide how to store overlapping regions of one image.

  • rects: col.Iterable[Rect] - Regions.
  • max_waste: float - Allowed unused share of a merged group.

Returns: dict[Rect, Rect] - Every region mapped to the region it's stored as (which contains it).

Regions overlapping each other (directly or through others) form groups. A group is stored as its bounding rectangle when that adds at most max_waste times the group's covered area of pixels nobody uses. Otherwise its regions are stored apart, except regions lying fully within another, which are stored as part of it.

View source 
def merge_regions(
    rects: col.Iterable[Rect], max_waste: float
) -> dict[Rect, Rect]:
    """Decide how to store overlapping regions of one image.

    Regions overlapping each other (directly or through others) form
    groups. A group is stored as its bounding rectangle when that adds at
    most ``max_waste`` times the group's covered area of pixels nobody uses.
    Otherwise its regions are stored apart, except regions lying fully
    within another, which are stored as part of it.

    :param rects: Regions.
    :param max_waste: Allowed unused share of a merged group.
    :return: Every region mapped to the region it's stored as (which
      contains it).
    """
    unique = sorted(set(rects), key=lambda r: (-r[2] * r[3], r))
    # union-find over overlapping regions
    parent: list[int] = list(range(len(unique)))

    order = sorted(range(len(unique)), key=lambda i: unique[i][0])
    for pos, i in enumerate(order):
        a = unique[i]
        for j in order[pos + 1 :]:
            b = unique[j]
            if b[0] >= a[0] + a[2]:
                break
            if rect_overlaps(a, b):
                parent[_find(parent, i)] = _find(parent, j)

    groups: dict[int, list[Rect]] = {}
    for i, rect in enumerate(unique):
        groups.setdefault(_find(parent, i), []).append(rect)

    stored: dict[Rect, Rect] = {}
    for members in groups.values():
        bounds = rect_bounds(members)
        covered = union_area(members)
        if bounds[2] * bounds[3] - covered <= max_waste * covered:
            for rect in members:
                stored[rect] = bounds
            continue
        # largest first, so containers are known before what they contain
        tops: list[Rect] = []
        for rect in members:
            container = next((t for t in tops if rect_contains(t, rect)), None)
            if container is None:
                tops.append(rect)
                container = rect
            stored[rect] = container
    return stored

def grid_rects(
    cells: col.Mapping[tuple[int, int], K],
) -> list[tuple[int, int, int, int, K]]:

Merge grid cells with equal keys into rectangles.

  • cells: col.Mapping[tuple[int, int], K] - Cells (column, row) and their keys; missing cells are empty.

Returns: list[tuple[int, int, int, int, K]] - Rectangles (column, row, columns, rows, key).

Greedy: from the top left, a rectangle grows right as long as cells have the same key, then down as long as whole rows below do.

View source 
def grid_rects[K](
    cells: col.Mapping[tuple[int, int], K],
) -> list[tuple[int, int, int, int, K]]:
    """Merge grid cells with equal keys into rectangles.

    Greedy: from the top left, a rectangle grows right as long as cells have
    the same key, then down as long as whole rows below do.

    :param cells: Cells (column, row) and their keys; missing cells are
      empty.
    :return: Rectangles (column, row, columns, rows, key).
    """
    used: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
    rects: list[tuple[int, int, int, int, K]] = []
    for cx, cy in sorted(cells, key=operator.itemgetter(1, 0)):
        if (cx, cy) in used:
            continue
        key = cells[cx, cy]

        def free(x: int, y: int, key: K = key) -> bool:
            return (
                (x, y) not in used and (x, y) in cells and cells[x, y] == key
            )

        width = 1
        while free(cx + width, cy):
            width += 1
        height = 1
        while all(free(cx + dx, cy + height) for dx in range(width)):
            height += 1
        for dy in range(height):
            used.update((cx + dx, cy + dy) for dx in range(width))
        rects.append((cx, cy, width, height, key))
    return rects

def format_line(violation: Violation, project: Project) -> str:
    """Format violation as a single line.

    Uses ``<file>:<line>:<column> (<asset>) - <message>`` format, omitting
    parts that aren't set.
    """
    parts: list[str] = []
    loc = violation.location
    if loc is not None:
        parts.append(
            f'{project.rel(loc.file)}:{loc.loc_line}:{loc.loc_column}'
        )
    if violation.asset is not None:
        asset = format_asset(violation.asset)
        parts.append(f'({asset})' if parts else asset)
    if violation.message:
        parts.append(f'- {violation.message}' if parts else violation.message)
    return ' '.join(parts)

def format_excerpt(location: Location, project: Project) -> str:
    """Format a few source lines around the location, marking the column."""
    lines = project.lines(location.file)
    first = max(0, location.loc_line - 3)
    last = min(len(lines), location.loc_line + 3)
    output: list[str] = []
    for num in range(first + 1, last + 1):
        output.append(f'{num:>4}|{lines[num - 1]}')
        if num == location.loc_line:
            output.append('    ' + ' ' * location.loc_column + '^')
    return '\n'.join(output)

    violations: col.Iterable[Violation],
    project: Project,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> str:

Format violations into a report.

  • violations: col.Iterable[Violation] - Violations to report.
  • project: Project - Linted project, used for formatting paths.
  • verbose: bool = False - Whether to include source excerpts.

Returns: str - Report text, empty if there are no violations.

Violations are grouped by rule, then by their group, and sorted by asset and location.

View source 
def format_report(
    violations: col.Iterable[Violation],
    project: Project,
    *,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Format violations into a report.

    Violations are grouped by rule, then by their ``group``, and sorted by
    asset and location.

    :param violations: Violations to report.
    :param project: Linted project, used for formatting paths.
    :param verbose: Whether to include source excerpts.
    :return: Report text, empty if there are no violations.
    """
    by_rule: dict[Rule, list[Violation]] = {}
    for violation in violations:
        by_rule.setdefault(violation.rule, []).append(violation)

    blocks: list[str] = []
    for rule, rule_violations in sorted(
        by_rule.items(), key=lambda item: item[0].code
    ):
        rule_violations.sort(key=lambda v: _sort_key(v, project))
        count = f'{len(rule_violations)} {_SEVERITY_WORDS[rule.severity]}'
        lines = [f'=== {rule.code} ({rule.title}): {count}']
        group: str | None = None
        for violation in rule_violations:
            if violation.group and violation.group != group:
                lines.append(f'\n--- {violation.group} ---')
            group = violation.group
            lines.append(f'  {format_line(violation, project)}')
            lines.extend(f'    {detail}' for detail in violation.details)
            if verbose and violation.location is not None:
                lines.append(format_excerpt(violation.location, project))
        blocks.append('\n'.join(lines))
    return '\n\n'.join(blocks)

View source 
def model_text(quads: col.Sequence[Quad]) -> str:
    """Format quads as a GameMaker model (``d3d_model_save`` format).

    Every quad is two triangles of a triangle list, in the given order.
    """
    lines: list[str] = []
    vertices = 0
    for quad in quads:
        if vertices == 0:
            lines.append(_line(_PRIMITIVE_BEGIN, _TRIANGLE_LIST))
        corners = (
            (quad.x1, quad.y1, quad.u1, quad.v1),
            (quad.x2, quad.y1, quad.u2, quad.v1),
            (quad.x1, quad.y2, quad.u1, quad.v2),
            (quad.x1, quad.y2, quad.u1, quad.v2),
            (quad.x2, quad.y1, quad.u2, quad.v1),
            (quad.x2, quad.y2, quad.u2, quad.v2),
        )
        lines.extend(
            _line(_VERTEX_TEXTURE_COLOR, x, y, 0, u, v, quad.color, quad.alpha)
            for x, y, u, v in corners
        )
        vertices += 6
        if vertices + 6 > MAX_PRIMITIVE_VERTICES:
            lines.append(_line(_PRIMITIVE_END))
            vertices = 0
    if vertices:
        lines.append(_line(_PRIMITIVE_END))
    return '\r\n'.join(('100', str(len(lines)), *lines, ''))

    changes made to the files afterwards.
    """

    def __init__(self, root: Path) -> None:
        """Initialize the project.

        :param root: Absolute path to the project root, where the ``.gm82``
          file is stored.
        """
        if not root.is_absolute():
            raise ValueError(f"Expected an absolute path, got '{root}'")
        if not root.is_dir():
            raise NotADirectoryError(root)
        self.root = root
        self._text: dict[Path, str] = {}
        self._line_maps: dict[Path, LineMap] = {}
        self._lines: dict[Path, tuple[str, ...]] = {}

    def rel(self, path: Path) -> str:
        """Convert absolute path in the project to POSIX relative path."""
        if not path.is_absolute():
            raise ValueError(f"Expected an absolute path, got '{path}'")
        if not path.is_relative_to(self.root):
            raise ValueError(f"Path '{path}' isn't in root {self.root}")
        return path.relative_to(self.root).as_posix()

    def try_rel(self, path: Path) -> str:
        """Try to convert absolute path in the project to POSIX relative path.

        If impossible, returns path as is.
        """
        if not path.is_absolute():
            raise ValueError(f"Expected an absolute path, got '{path}'")
        if not path.is_relative_to(self.root):
            return str(path)
        return path.relative_to(self.root).as_posix()

    def read(self, path: Path) -> str:
        """Read project's text file with caching."""
        if path in self._text:
            return self._text[path]
        if not path.is_absolute():
            raise ValueError(f"Expected an absolute path, got '{path}'")
        if not path.is_relative_to(self.root):
            raise ValueError(f"Path '{path}' isn't in root {self.root}")
        txt = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
        self._text[path] = txt
        return txt

    def line_map(self, path: Path) -> LineMap:
        """Read line map with caching."""
        if path not in self._line_maps:
            self._line_maps[path] = LineMap.from_text(self.read(path))
        return self._line_maps[path]

    def lines(self, path: Path) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Read lines with caching."""
        if path not in self._lines:
            self._lines[path] = tuple(self.read(path).splitlines())
        return self._lines[path]

View source 
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Tile:
    """Room tile, as stored in a tile layer file.

    Draws region ``left, top, width, height`` of background ``bg`` at
    ``x, y``, scaled by ``xscale, yscale`` (negative scales mirror).
    """

    bg: str
    x: float
    y: float
    left: int
    top: int
    width: int
    height: int
    # meaning unknown, kept as is
    flag: str
    xscale: float
    yscale: float
    # alpha in the highest byte, blend color (BGR) below
    color: int

    @property
    def alpha(self) -> float:
        """Tile's alpha (0-1)."""
        return (self.color >> 24) / 255

    @property
    def blend(self) -> int:
        """Tile's blend color (BGR)."""
        return self.color & 0xFFFFFF

    def region(self) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
        """Background region: left, top, width, height."""
        return self.left, self.top, self.width, self.height

    def bounds(self) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
        """Drawn area in the room: left, top, right, bottom."""
        x2 = self.x + self.width * self.xscale
        y2 = self.y + self.height * self.yscale
        return (
            min(self.x, x2),
            min(self.y, y2),
            max(self.x, x2),
            max(self.y, y2),
        )

    def contains(self, px: float, py: float) -> bool:
        """Check whether a point lies within the drawn area.

        Edges count as inside, so this errs on the side of a match.
        """
        left, top, right, bottom = self.bounds()
        return left <= px <= right and top <= py <= bottom

    def sub(self, dx: int, dy: int, width: int, height: int) -> Tile:
        """Get a tile drawing a part of this tile's region at the same place.

        :param dx: Part's offset from the region's left.
        :param dy: Part's offset from the region's top.
        :param width: Part's width.
        :param height: Part's height.
        """
        return dataclasses.replace(
            self,
            x=_clean(self.x + dx * self.xscale),
            y=_clean(self.y + dy * self.yscale),
            left=self.left + dx,
            top=self.top + dy,
            width=width,
            height=height,
        )

    def format(self) -> str:
        """Format as a tile layer line."""
        return ','.join((
            self.bg,
            format_number(self.x),
            format_number(self.y),
            str(self.left),
            str(self.top),
            str(self.width),
            str(self.height),
            self.flag,
            format_number(self.xscale),
            format_number(self.yscale),
            str(self.color),
        ))

def parse_line(line: str) -> Tile:
    """Parse a tile layer line."""
    fields = line.split(',')
    if len(fields) != 11:
        raise ValueError(f'Malformed tile line: {line!r}')
    return Tile(
        bg=fields[0],
        x=float(fields[1]),
        y=float(fields[2]),
        left=int(fields[3]),
        top=int(fields[4]),
        width=int(fields[5]),
        height=int(fields[6]),
        flag=fields[7],
        xscale=float(fields[8]),
        yscale=float(fields[9]),
        color=int(fields[10]),
    )

items.title: CLS ScanCache
items.text:
Per-file cache of reference scan results.

A file's matches are reused while its stat is unchanged and the set of scanned names stays the same (see set_names). Entries of files that weren't looked up since the last save are dropped on save.

View source 
class ScanCache:
    """Per-file cache of reference scan results.

    A file's matches are reused while its stat is unchanged and the set of
    scanned names stays the same (see ``set_names``). Entries of files that
    weren't looked up since the last save are dropped on save.
    """

    def __init__(self, cache_file: Path) -> None:
        """Initialize the cache, loading the cache file if it exists.

        :param cache_file: Path to the cache file.
        """
        self.cache_file = cache_file
        self.names_key = ''
        self._entries: dict[str, tuple[FileStat, tuple[FileMatch, ...]]] = {}
        self._used: set[str] = set()
        self._dirty = False

        if not cache_file.exists():
            return
        with cache_file.open('r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            raw = json.load(f)
        if raw.get('version') != CACHE_VERSION:
            return
        self.names_key = raw['names_key']
        for file, ((mtime, size, ino), matches) in raw['files'].items():
            self._entries[file] = (
                (mtime, size, ino),
                tuple(
                    FileMatch(idx, line, column, target, tuple(contexts))
                    for idx, line, column, target, contexts in matches
                ),
            )

    def set_names(self, names_key: str) -> None:
        """Set the key of scanned names, e.g. a hash of all asset names.

        Entries scanned for different names are dropped.
        """
        if names_key != self.names_key:
            self.names_key = names_key
            self._entries.clear()
            self._dirty = True

    def get(self, path: Path, stat: FileStat) -> tuple[FileMatch, ...] | None:
        """Get file's cached matches, ``None`` if missing or outdated.

        :param path: Scanned file.
        :param stat: File's current stat.
        """
        key = str(path)
        self._used.add(key)
        entry = self._entries.get(key)
        if entry is None or entry[0] != stat:
            return None
        return entry[1]

    def put(
        self, path: Path, stat: FileStat, matches: col.Iterable[FileMatch]
    ) -> None:
        """Store file's matches.

        :param path: Scanned file.
        :param stat: File's stat, taken before reading it.
        :param matches: Matches found in the file.
        """
        key = str(path)
        self._used.add(key)
        self._dirty = True
        if stat[0] > time.time_ns() - RACY_WINDOW_NS:
            # too recent to trust the stat, rescan next time
            self._entries.pop(key, None)
            return
        self._entries[key] = (stat, tuple(matches))

    def save(self) -> None:
        """Save the cache, if anything changed."""
        unused = self._entries.keys() - self._used
        for key in unused:
            del self._entries[key]
        self._dirty = self._dirty or bool(unused)
        self._used.clear()
        if not self._dirty:
            return

        data = {
            'version': CACHE_VERSION,
            'names_key': self.names_key,
            'files': {
                key: (
                    stat,
                    [
                        (m.idx, m.line, m.column, m.target, m.contexts)
                        for m in matches
                    ],
                )
                for key, (stat, matches) in self._entries.items()
            },
        }
        temp_file = self.cache_file.with_suffix('.tmp')
        # dumps, unlike dump, uses the C encoder, which is a lot faster
        temp_file.write_text(
            json.dumps(data, separators=(',', ':')), encoding='utf-8'
        )
        temp_file.replace(self.cache_file)
        self._dirty = False

def scan(
    text: str,
    search_iter: col.Iterator[tuple[int, str]],
) -> col.Iterator[DependencyMatch]:
    """Scans a single file's text for asset dependencies.

    Search iterator may be acquired from ahocorasick's ``Automaton.iter(text)``
    :param text: Text to scan.
    :param search_iter: Iterator of all search matches (end_index, found_word)
     across the given text.
    :return: Dependency edges.
    """
    if '//!clunkster: ignore' in text:
        # don't process this file
        return

    gml_index = my_parse_gml.GmlIndex.from_text(text)

    for end_idx, target_asset in search_iter:
        start_idx = end_idx - len(target_asset) + 1

        # detect if this target is explicitly formatted as a string literal
        is_string_ref = target_asset.startswith(('"', "'"))

        # check if whole identifier
        if not is_string_ref:
            if start_idx > 0:
                prev_char = text[start_idx - 1]
                if prev_char.isalnum() or prev_char == '_':
                    # allow the match if it is strictly part of an event header
                    if (
                        prev_char == '_'
                        and text[start_idx - 18 : start_idx]
                        == '#define Collision_'
                    ):
                        pass
                    else:
                        continue
            if end_idx + 1 < len(text):
                next_char = text[end_idx + 1]
                if next_char.isalnum() or next_char == '_':
                    continue

        # check if symbol is not inside ignored syntax
        if not is_string_ref and gml_index.is_ignored_at(start_idx):
            continue

        contexts = gml_index.get_contexts_at(start_idx)

        yield DependencyMatch(
            idx=start_idx,
            target=target_asset,
            contexts=contexts,
        )

def apply_hints(row: dict[str, Any], hints: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Apply type hints to a dict."""
    for field_name, field_type in hints.items():
        if field_name not in row:
            raise ValueError(f'Missing field: {field_name}')

        value = row[field_name]

        if field_type is int:
            row[field_name] = int(value)
        elif field_type is float:
            row[field_name] = float(value)
        elif field_type is str:
            row[field_name] = value
        else:
            raise TypeError(
                f'Unsupported type {field_type!r} for field {field_name}'
            )
